title: EFC-C: A Thermodynamic Framework for Cognitive Entropy and Psychiatric Biomarkers
description: Introduces EFC-C, a thermodynamic framework that models the brain as an open system governed by entropy-gradient dynamics. It defines a scalar neural entropy production rate and a gradient tensor over the connectome, yielding three falsifiable predictions on hub-to-periphery entropy topology, disorder-specific gradient signatures, and a cognitive threshold. The paper shows qualitative consistency with published EEG/fMRI findings and outlines a prospective validation protocol.

total_entropy_production_rate.description: Defines the total neural entropy production rate as the spatial integral of local entropy production density over brain regions, summed across a partition of the connectome.

disorder_gradient_tensor.description: Characterizes psychiatric pathology as a deformation of the entropy-flow gradient tensor relative to healthy topology, measurable from resting-state EEG/fMRI-derived entropy maps.

key_results.main_finding: EFC-C predicts a centrifugal hub-to-periphery entropy topology, disorder-specific gradient signatures, and a cognitive entropy-production threshold, and shows qualitative consistency with published EEG/fMRI literature.
parameters_tested: total neural entropy production rate (\dot S_neural)
datasets_used: Published EEG/fMRI findings cited by the paper (e.g., Rosas 2023; Carhart-Harris 2018; Creel & Hartman 2025; Noroozi 2025; Pan 2025)

sealed_predictions.statement: In healthy resting brains, entropy production is maximal in integrative hubs (e.g., DMN) and decreases centrifugally toward primary sensory cortices.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Resting-state EEG/fMRI mapping (e.g., Lempel–Ziv complexity, multiscale entropy) showing sensory-first maxima or a centripetal gradient across large cohorts with robust estimators.

sealed_predictions.statement: Psychiatric disorders exhibit disorder-specific gradient deformations: schizophrenia shows elevated anterior entropy and fragmented hub gradients; MDD shows reduced magnitude with posterior bias; ADHD shows fragmented gradient topology.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Case-control EEG/fMRI studies across large cohorts failing to find these specific gradient signatures (or showing opposite patterns) with preregistered pipelines and cross-modal replication.

sealed_predictions.statement: There exists a system-dependent entropy-production threshold \(\dot S_*\) below which coordinated cognition degrades or fails.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Anesthesia/DoC datasets showing intact cognition with persistently sub-threshold entropy production (or unresponsive states with sustained supra-threshold entropy) across multiple estimators and modalities.

kill_criteria: KC1: High-quality resting-state EEG/fMRI consistently shows maximal entropy in primary sensory cortices with a stable centripetal gradient toward hubs in healthy adults, contradicting the predicted centrifugal hub-to-periphery topology.

KC2: In preregistered, multi-cohort analyses, schizophrenia does not exhibit elevated anterior entropy or hub-gradient fragmentation, and MDD does not show reduced magnitude with posterior bias; instead results consistently show no deformation or the opposite patterns under robust entropy estimators.

KC3: Across anesthesia and disorders-of-consciousness datasets, participants display sustained, verified cognitive function while neural entropy production remains persistently below any proposed \(\dot S_*\), or conversely show persistent unresponsiveness with clearly supra-threshold entropy.

KC4: Cross-modal and cross-estimator robustness failure: independently derived \nabla\dot S fields from EEG and fMRI (e.g., MSE, LZC, spectral-entropy variants) are systematically inconsistent beyond methodological uncertainty, preventing stable tensor reconstruction.

KC5: A magnitude-only (scalar) entropy model fully explains state and disorder data and provides superior predictive accuracy to EFC-C’s gradient model across held-out datasets, leaving no added value for topology or gradient direction.
abstract: EFC-C models the brain as an open thermodynamic system governed by entropy-gradient dynamics. The framework produces a scalar observable S_dot_neural (total neural entropy production rate) and a gradient tensor nabla S_dot encoding directional entropy flow. Three falsifiable predictions distinguish EFC-C from the Entropic Brain Hypothesis: (1) centrifugal hub-to-periphery gradient, (2) disorder-specific gradient inversions, (3) entropy threshold for cognitive function.

core_postulate.equation: S_dot_neural = sum_i integral(s_dot_i dV) over regions R_i
core_postulate.gradient_tensor: nabla S_dot encodes directional structure of entropy flow across connectome
core_postulate.disorder_gradient: Delta nabla S_disorder = nabla S_patient - nabla S_healthy

comparison_with_existing.key_distinction: EBH is the scalar projection of the more complete EFC-C tensor field

predictions.title: Topological entropy structure
predictions.prediction: Entropy production highest in DMN hubs, decreasing centrifugally toward sensory cortices
predictions.consistency: Consistent with fMRI: Lempel-Ziv complexity and MSE highest in association cortices and DMN

predictions.title: Disorder-specific gradient signatures
predictions.prediction: Schizophrenia: elevated anterior entropy, fragmented hub gradient. MDD: reduced magnitude, posterior bias. ADHD: fragmented gradient topology.
predictions.consistency_mdd: Lower MSE in left frontal, reduced EEG microstate complexity [8]

predictions.title: Entropy threshold for cognitive function
predictions.prediction: Onset of productive cognition requires S_dot_neural > S_dot_star
predictions.consistency: Loss of Lempel-Ziv complexity below critical level predicts unresponsive states [2]

limitations: No direct model fit (qualitative consistency only)
Parameter underdetermination (bridge theory from EFC cosmological to neural not derived)
Gradient measurement requires careful entropy estimator, scale, and parcellation choices
next_steps: Fit EFC-C gradient model to open resting-state fMRI (HCP, OpenNeuro)
Derive formal bridge from EFC cosmological entropy equations to neural s_dot_i
Test P2 differential: schizophrenia vs MDD classification using gradient features
AIC comparison against pure-EBH scalar model

references.citation: Carhart-Harris et al., Front. Hum. Neurosci. 8, 20 (2014)
